claim: Energy needs are estimates and should include uncertainty
evidence_source: NASEM Dietary Reference Intakes for Energy, DOI 10.17226/26818
limitations: Population equations do not measure an individual's expenditure
implementation_implication: Version the equation and calibrate with observed trends

claim: Healthy plans should prioritise adequacy, balance, moderation and diversity
limitations: Not a personalised clinical prescription
implementation_implication: Add diet-quality constraints beyond calories

claim: At least 400 g fruit/vegetables and 25 g naturally occurring fibre are adult public-health targets
limitations: Individual clinical needs can differ
implementation_implication: Track produce and fibre completeness

claim: Fat should generally remain within a healthy reference range
limitations: National guidance and individual needs vary
implementation_implication: Use ranges; do not force unexplained 30/34% constants

claim: Weight-loss diets should be flexible, individualised, nutritionally balanced and create an energy deficit
limitations: Guideline assumes professional support and UK care context
implementation_implication: Preserve deficit logic but do not claim one universal percentage

claim: Low-energy diets of 800–1200 kcal/day are specialist interventions, not ordinary self-service defaults
population: defined adults with obesity or overweight plus type 2 diabetes
limitations: Not a universal minimum-intake rule
implementation_implication: Do not use 1200/1500 floors as the only safety mechanism

claim: Static 7700 kcal/kg predictions overstate long-term precision
evidence_source: Hall dynamic-weight literature; NIDDK Body Weight Planner research
limitations: Dynamic model implementation is more complex
implementation_implication: Do not promise timelines; use trends

claim: Resistance exercise is necessary for meaningful hypertrophy
evidence_source: Academy/DC/ACSM Nutrition and Athletic Performance; ISSN protein stand
limitations: Training quality and individual response vary
implementation_implication: Require training questions and explicit explanation

claim: About 1.6 g/kg/day protein is a defensible muscle-gain default
limitations: Average breakpoint; older adults and individuals may differ
implementation_implication: Candidate default 1.6 g/kg/day after screening

claim: 1.4–2.0 g/kg/day protein is sufficient for most exercising people
limitations: Sports population; society position; not renal-disease guidance
implementation_implication: Use bounded personalisation, never for excluded conditions

claim: Total daily protein matters more than rigid timing; 0.25–0.40 g/kg per feeding every 3–4 h is optional guidance
limitations: Timing evidence is less decisive than total intake
implementation_implication: Offer optional distribution, not mandatory meal frequency

claim: No universal optimal energy surplus for hypertrophy has been validated
limitations: Few direct controlled trials
implementation_implication: Use conservative adaptive trial policy; do not hard-code before approval

claim: A 500 kcal/day surplus with supervised resistance training produced about 0.22 kg/week gain in one trial
limitations: Small sample, ten weeks, supervised training, not general population
implementation_implication: Evidence example only; not a universal prescription

claim: Unintentional loss, BMI <18.5, prolonged low intake and swallowing/GI concerns require professional assessment
limitations: Clinical guideline, not consumer-app validation
implementation_implication: Hard exclusion and referral flow

claim: Refeeding-risk criteria require skilled clinical care
limitations: Requires clinical labs/history not fully available to app
implementation_implication: Hard stop; never generate ordinary plan

claim: Food composition must distinguish raw/cooked data, yields, retention and provenance
limitations: National data access/licensing varies
implementation_implication: Create structured provenance-aware food and recipe model

claim: Iranian foods should preferentially use a national table when licensing and data access permit
evidence_source: FAO listing: Iranian Food Composition Table 2017
limitations: Restricted access and licence not yet verified
implementation_implication: Do not copy values until rights and source fields are confirmed

claim: Supplements are optional and require assessment; contamination and harm are real risks
limitations: Elite-sport framing; general users still share product-quality risks
implementation_implication: Keep supplements separate and non-mandatory

claim: A single blood-pressure reading must not be used by the product to diagnose hypertension
evidence_source: WHO Hypertension 2025; AHA/ACC High Blood Pressure Guideline 2025
study_type: global fact sheet and clinical guideline
limitations: Classification thresholds differ and measurement context matters
implementation_implication: Collect repeated-reading context and show no diagnosis

claim: Blood pressure above 180/120 mm Hg requires prompt clinical assessment; symptoms may indicate an emergency
limitations: Device error and symptom context must be considered
implementation_implication: Hard block ordinary planning and route by symptom status

claim: Adults should generally consume less than 2000 mg sodium per day
limitations: Population target; individual restrictions vary; current catalogue lacks sodium
implementation_implication: Use as reference only until food sodium data is complete

claim: Prediabetes laboratory reference criteria are A1C 5.7–6.4%, fasting glucose 100–125 mg/dL, or 2-hour OGTT 140–199 mg/dL
evidence_source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, section 2
limitations: Not a consumer diagnosis; confirmation and laboratory context matter
implementation_implication: Educational reference and professional-review prompt only

claim: Glucose below 70 mg/dL is clinically important hypoglycaemia and below 54 mg/dL is level 2
evidence_source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, section 6
limitations: Medication, symptoms, and device accuracy matter
implementation_implication: Block ordinary planning when current/recurrent and escalate severe events

claim: There is no ideal universal macronutrient percentage for diabetes prevention or management
evidence_source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, sections 3 and 5
limitations: Individual MNT is recommended
implementation_implication: Do not create a fixed diabetic macro formula

claim: LDL-C and non-HDL-C goals depend on cardiovascular risk and clinical context
limitations: Requires risk assessment and clinical history
implementation_implication: Do not show a universal LDL target

claim: Pancreatitis risk increases at triglycerides at or above 500 mg/dL and is particularly high at or above 1000 mg/dL
limitations: Fasting status and secondary causes require clinical evaluation
implementation_implication: Professional-review block at 500; high-priority assessment at 1000

claim: A heart-healthy dietary pattern replaces saturated-fat sources with unsaturated-fat sources and emphasises minimally processed foods
evidence_source: AHA Dietary Guidance to Improve Cardiovascular Health
limitations: Not a substitute for disease-specific MNT
implementation_implication: Add qualitative cardiometabolic compatibility after food-data migration
